description:
FILED s450u (Opus, round 8 agent U) while shipping #560.

`~/.pcl-cache/proto/` (Pl::ProtoCache) has NO pruning.  An entry's filename
carries a hash of the module's path+mtime+size, the cache generation, the
COMPILER stamp (every Pl/**.pm's mtime+size) and the PPI/perl versions, so an
entry becomes UNREACHABLE the moment any of those changes -- correct, and
never stale -- but it is not removed.  On a development machine that means a
new full set per compiler edit; measured s450u, an entry is ~1-5 KB and a
full cpan-t census pass writes ~100 of them, so a set is a few hundred KB and
a busy week is tens of MB.  Not a correctness problem and not urgent.

WHAT TO DO: the runtime already has the policy for its sibling cache --
`*pcl-cache-max-age*` (7 days) and `p-prune-cache` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp --
so the answer is that policy, not a new one.  The one thing to get right is
CONCURRENCY: `prove -j8` and the census run many transpiles at once, so a
prune must not unlink an entry a reader is opening (open-then-unlink is safe
on Linux; the reader's fd survives).  Cheapest shape: on a STORE, once per
process at most, if a `.last-prune` marker in the directory is older than a
day, rewrite the marker (atomically, temp+rename, so only one process wins)
and unlink entries whose mtime is older than the max age.

`pcl --clear-cache` already removes the whole directory and reports the count
(s450u), so a user has the manual escape today.

=== DONE (s470by) ===

Folded into #1300 item B (F2, the prune).  p-cleanup-old-cache now walks
<cache>/proto/ as well as <cache>/modules/ -- the prototype memo had never been
pruned by anything -- and the rule is LAST USE, not write date: an entry that is
used is re-stamped by %p-note-cache-use and anything nothing reached for 30 days
(*pcl-cache-max-age*, was 7) is deleted.

MEASURED, and the measurement is why the scan is claimed once a day rather than
run on every miss: modules/ 590 files 7.0 ms + proto/ 1112 files 14.0 ms = 21 ms
per scan, warm; %p-claim-prune publishes a .last-prune stamp (temp + rename(2)).
The touch itself is one utime(2) = 0.0020 ms, and the warm A/B is flat (use Moo
435/438 -> 455/421 ms, use JSON::PP 1476/1422 -> 1396/1399 ms, best-of-5 x2).

Smoke-tested by hand and then guarded: the prune deletes a 40-day-old module
entry AND a 40-day-old proto entry and leaves the fresh one; the touch fires at
5 days and not at 1 hour.  Guard rows in Pl/t/cache-surface-01.t.
subject: ~/.pcl-cache/proto has no pruning: an entry is unreachable the moment the compiler stamp or generation changes, but never removed
